A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same batching study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices—A–I in v3 and A–J in v4—are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original batching and gradient-update timing measurements, learning curves, and statistical comparisons on QM9 and AFLOW, including Figure 4, Table 1, and Appendices G–I.

after.justification: V4 reports original timing and learning results on QM9 and AFLOW, including Figure 5, Table 1, learning curves, and statistical analyses in Appendices I–J.

M1.justification: V4 Algorithm 3 adds batch reset, carryover of the overflowing graph, and final-batch output absent from v3 Algorithm 1. These are limited revisions to the stated pseudocode. The batching strategies and GNN models remain unchanged; changes to the experimental implementation are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use QM9 molecular internal-energy prediction and AFLOW crystal-enthalpy prediction. The newly displayed AFLOW results concern an already evaluated dataset and task, rather than expanded coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain dynamic, static-64, and static-2^N batching, with static-constant included in the same Table 1 subsets. The learning comparisons also retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: The four batch sizes, model sizes, graph preprocessing, two-million-step main experiments, and 100,000-step CPU experiments are retained. CPU-only evaluation already appeared in v3 Appendix E. V4's explicit exclusion of budget-estimation time clarifies the existing timing scope.

E4.justification: New Appendix D and Figure 11 examine how AFLOW timing rankings evolve with training duration, complementing the retained QM9 trajectory. Existing mean-versus-median, CPU, and multi-GPU feasibility analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 8 replaces the main uncorrected Student's t-test analysis with Mann–Whitney U tests, Bonferroni adjustment within model/dataset families, and an adjusted-p threshold of 0.05. This substantially changes the inferential framework. Ten repetitions remain unchanged, and the earlier t-tests are retained in Appendix I.

E6.justification: V4 adds AFLOW timing and RMSE trajectories and additional statistical heatmaps. Its revised analysis reports no significant QM9 differences and one SchNet/AFLOW/batch-size-16 configuration with adjusted p approximately 0.0022, whereas v3 highlighted several QM9 t-test differences. Table 1 and the headline timing findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The SchNet, MPEU, and PaiNN equations (1–7) move from v3 Appendix A into v4 Section 3 without substantive mathematical changes. Expanded graph notation does not introduce new theoretical results, assumptions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction and discussion narrow the learning-difference claim from several configurations to one SchNet/AFLOW/batch-size-16 configuration. The 2.7x and 12.5x speedup claims and recommendation favoring dynamic batching are retained.

C2.justification: V4 links the isolated AFLOW learning difference specifically to gradient noise from small batches in heavy-tailed data, refining v3's broader fewer-labeled-graphs explanation. It also explains the normality and multiple-testing concerns motivating the revised statistical analysis.

D1.justification: V4 explicitly documents excluded budget-estimation time, expands batch/padding details, and includes Mann–Whitney heatmaps in its availability statement. It also replaces 'single CPU core' with the less precise 'single CPU'. Algorithms 1–2 inconsistently use the real-graph limit as the final padded graph count.

R1.justification: V4 adds Mann and Whitney (1947), Dunn (1961), Demšar (2006), and Wasserstein and Lazar (2016) to support the statistical analysis. The batching-related research positioning and novelty claims otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 substantially reorganizes the exposition: model descriptions and appendix equations enter the preliminaries, batching receives a dedicated section with rewritten pseudocode and expanded explanations, and the earlier t-test discussion moves into an appendix.

P2.justification: V4 adds a batching schematic, AFLOW trajectories, and statistical heatmaps. It redraws the main timing figure with revised panel framing and spacing, relocates and enlarges retained displays, separates previously combined displays, and changes the document's typography and page layout.

improvement.justification: V4's multiplicity-corrected nonparametric analysis makes the learning claim more defensible than v3's uncorrected t-tests. The schematic and additional AFLOW plots improve clarity and inspectability while retaining the core timing evidence. The graph-count inconsistency in the expanded padding pseudocode limits the reproducibility gain.
